extra_misconceptions.fact: Shoe soles can still conduct current or fail to stop skin contact, so shut off power first or use a dry nonconductive object.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubber-soled sneakers provide enough insulation to let you safely grab a person who is in contact with a live household wire.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High voltage bridges tires easily, and stepping out creates a lethal path through your body between the car and the earth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubber tires insulate a car completely from a downed power line, making it safe to step out onto the pavement normally.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wall switches usually control only ceiling fixtures or half-switched outlets, so you must trip the circuit breaker or main switch.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Flipping a wall light switch to the off position cuts all electrical power to a frayed appliance cord plugged into that room.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wide steps create a dangerous voltage difference between your feet, so shuffle with both feet together or hop away slowly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Running with long strides away from a downed power line gets you out of the ground voltage gradient zone with the least risk.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your body if you touch both the car frame and the ground at once while escaping a vehicle on a downed power line?
Why is it dangerous to use a wet wooden broom handle or damp rope to pull a shock victim away from an energized household wire?
Which physical indicator on a home service panel distinguishes the main disconnect breaker from individual branch circuit breakers?
In what manner must you move your feet across the ground after jumping clear of a car energized by a fallen overhead power line?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Power strips only add outlets without raising circuit capacity, and plugging them into ungrounded adapters removes ground safety.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A three-prong power strip adds surge protection and increases the safe amperage capacity of an older two-slot wall receptacle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Internal trip mechanisms can corrode and stick over time, so every GFCI receptacle should be tested monthly with its test button.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing the test button on a GFCI outlet is unnecessary as long as the small green indicator light on the faceplate stays lit.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Extension cords are rated only for temporary portable use and degrade or overheat when used as permanent household wiring.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heavy-duty orange extension cords can safely replace permanent wall wiring if they are tucked neatly along the room baseboards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Warmth, discoloration, or buzzing at a switch signals loose terminals or overloaded contacts that can start an electrical fire.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Warmth or a faint buzzing sound at a wall switch is normal whenever several high-wattage lamps are turned on in the same room.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the insulation on an extension cord when it is run underneath a heavy area rug or pinched inside a doorway?
Which physical indicator on a wall receptacle or faceplate warns you that internal wiring connections may be loose and arcing?
Where should a Scout verify that Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter outlets are installed and tested during a home safety audit?
Why is it dangerous to screw a 100-watt incandescent bulb into an enclosed ceiling fixture rated for a maximum of 60 watts?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bare wire turns touch each other and short-circuit the current across the nail, preventing the coil from forming a magnetic field.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bare copper wire wrapped tightly around a steel nail creates a stronger electromagnet because no plastic insulation blocks the flux.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only ferromagnetic metals like soft iron and steel concentrate magnetic flux lines strongly enough to multiply the coil field.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An aluminum bolt or brass rod makes just as strong a core for a battery-powered electromagnet as a soft iron or steel nail.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An energized coil has distinct north and south poles that repel the like pole of a compass needle or permanent bar magnet.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An electromagnet only attracts metal objects like paper clips and cannot push away the pole of a permanent bar magnet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hardened steel retains residual magnetism after power stops, whereas soft iron demagnetizes quickly when the circuit opens.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hardened high-carbon steel makes the ideal electromagnet core because it shuts off its magnetism the instant current stops.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the north and south poles of your homemade electromagnet when you reverse the battery wire connections?
Under what condition does wrapping more turns of insulated copper wire around an iron nail increase its magnetic lifting force?
Why is it dangerous to leave your electromagnet coil connected across a fresh lantern or D-cell battery for several minutes?
What measurement confirms that your nail core has reversed magnetic polarity when tested beside a permanent magnetic compass?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Solar cells produce direct current through the photovoltaic effect and require an inverter to convert it to alternating current.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Solar photovoltaic panels generate 120-volt alternating current directly from sunlight to run standard household appliances.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Transformers rely on a constantly changing magnetic field and only work with alternating current or pulsed current waveforms.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Transformers can step up the voltage of a 12-volt car battery directly without any switching electronics or inverter circuit.

extra_misconceptions.fact: In alternating current, electrons oscillate back and forth in place 60 times per second while electromagnetic energy moves fast.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Electrons in a 60-hertz household alternating current circuit travel all the way from the power plant to your lamp every second.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All three plants spin a turbine connected to an electromagnetic generator rotor to induce alternating current in stator coils.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Coal, nuclear, and hydroelectric power plants use completely different electrical mechanisms to generate grid alternating current.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is alternating current preferred over direct current for stepping voltage up and down across long-distance power grids?
What happens to electrons inside a copper wire coil when a permanent magnet is pushed rapidly back and forth through the center?
Which physical process produces direct current inside a flashlight battery compared to a rooftop solar photovoltaic panel?
Under what condition does stepping alternating current up to high voltage reduce power losses in utility transmission lines?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The battery supplies steady direct current, and the bell's own spring-loaded interrupter contact rapidly opens and closes the loop.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An electric bell rings continuously because the battery sends alternating pulses of current when you hold down the pushbutton.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pulling the armature forward breaks the contact point, cutting coil current so the spring snaps the striker back repeatedly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The iron armature stays pulled tightly against the electromagnet core for the entire time the doorbell button is held closed.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Without the return spring, the armature cannot snap back against the contact screw to re-close the circuit for the next strike.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Removing the spring from the armature arm makes the bell ring louder because the electromagnet faces less mechanical resistance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The gong is purely an acoustic resonator struck by the hammer, while current flows only through the coil and breaker contact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The metal gong must be wired directly into the battery circuit so current can flow through the bell dome when the hammer hits.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the electromagnet in a classic electric bell at the exact moment the striker arm pulls away from the contact screw?
Why does an electric bell strike the gong only once if you wire the battery return lead directly to the coil instead of the contact?
Which component in an electric bell diagram pulls the iron armature back to close the circuit after the electromagnet de-energizes?
Where must the pushbutton switch be placed in your series circuit diagram to control when the battery energizes the bell coil?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Overcurrent devices protect the house wiring inside walls from overheating and catching fire when excessive current is drawn.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Circuit breakers and fuses are installed primarily to protect sensitive electronics like televisions and computers from damage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A 20-ampere breaker on 14-gauge wire lets the conductor overheat past its safe insulation rating before the breaker ever trips.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Upgrading a tripping 15-ampere circuit breaker to a 20-ampere breaker safely lets you run more high-wattage kitchen appliances.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only active appliances draw full operating current, though devices in standby mode still consume a small phantom load in watts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every device plugged into a bedroom branch circuit draws its full nameplate wattage even when its power switch is turned off.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern breakers have trip-free internal mechanisms that still open under overload, and forcing a faulty circuit risks a fire.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding a circuit breaker toggle handle in the on position with tape prevents nuisance tripping during heavy appliance usage.

extra_socratic_questions: What total current in amperes is drawn when a 1,200-watt hair dryer and an 840-watt space heater run on one 120-volt branch circuit?
What happens to the metallic strip or fusible link inside an overcurrent device when circuit amperage exceeds its rated limit?
Why is it dangerous to replace a blown 15-ampere screw-in fuse with a 20-ampere fuse on a circuit wired with 14-gauge copper?
Where on a household appliance nameplate can you find the electrical values needed to calculate its current draw on a branch circuit?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Electricians often wire ceiling lights and wall receptacles on separate circuits so a tripped outlet breaker leaves lights on.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every electrical outlet and light switch located inside the same bedroom is always wired to a single branch circuit breaker.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Panel directory labels are frequently outdated after renovations, so you must verify each outlet and switch with a plug tester.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Handwritten room labels inside an older electrical panel door are always accurate enough to map a room diagram without testing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Household receptacles are wired in parallel so every outlet receives full 120-volt potential and operates independently.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wall outlets in a home branch circuit are wired in series so that electricity flows sequentially through every plugged-in lamp.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Split-wired duplex receptacles can be fed by two separate branch circuits, so both the top and bottom sockets must be tested.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: If the top socket of a duplex outlet turns off when a breaker trips, the bottom socket is guaranteed to be dead as well.

extra_socratic_questions: What procedure lets you verify which specific breaker in the service panel controls each duplex receptacle and ceiling light?
Why are the ceiling lights and wall outlets in a single room often split across two different branch breakers in the main panel?
Which standard schematic symbols on a floor plan distinguish a duplex wall receptacle from a single-pole wall switch and fixture?
What measurement or test confirms whether both sockets of a duplex wall outlet are permanently hot or controlled by a wall switch?

extra_misconceptions.fact: You always record the lower number that the dial pointer has just passed, unless it rests directly on a digit and check the next.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: When an analog electric meter pointer sits between 4 and 5, you round up to 5 if the pointer is more than halfway past the 4.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Adjacent gear-driven meter dials alternate between clockwise and counterclockwise rotation, so read each scale direction carefully.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every dial on a five-dial residential electric meter turns clockwise just like the hands on a standard analog wall clock.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Kilowatts measure the instantaneous rate of power demand, while kilowatt-hours measure total energy consumed over a period of time.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Kilowatts and kilowatt-hours measure the exact same electrical quantity on a household utility meter and monthly billing statement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Space heating, air conditioning, and electric water heaters consume far more household energy than lighting in almost every home.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Replacing incandescent bulbs with LEDs is the single biggest way to cut a home electric bill, ahead of heating and water heaters.

extra_socratic_questions: Which number should you record when a pointer on an analog dial electric meter stands directly between two digits on the scale?
Why do adjacent dials on a mechanical kilowatt-hour meter rotate in opposite clockwise and counterclockwise directions?
What formula converts a 1,500-watt space heater running for four hours per day into kilowatt-hours billed over thirty days?
How does the utility delivery and transmission fee on a monthly electric bill differ from the per-kilowatt-hour supply charge?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Watts measure the instantaneous rate of power use, whereas watt-hours measure total energy consumed over a period of time.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Watts and watt-hours measure the exact same electrical property and can be swapped on an appliance nameplate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Current is the flow of electrons through the conductor, while voltage is the potential difference pushing those charges.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Voltage flows through a copper wire just like water moving through a garden hose when a switch closes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An open circuit breaks the conducting path and stops current flow completely, whereas a short circuit spikes current and trips breakers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An open circuit causes circuit breakers to trip immediately because electricity spills out of the broken wire.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The neutral wire carries normal return current, while the ground wire only conducts fault current during an insulation failure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The bare copper ground wire carries normal return current back to the breaker panel whenever a lamp is turned on.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes a 100-watt bulb's instantaneous power draw from the watt-hours recorded on a utility meter?
Why is a low-resistance short circuit far more likely to melt wire insulation than an accidental open circuit?
What step must you take before touching ohmmeter probes to a resistor so circuit voltage does not damage the meter?
Under what condition can a bird perch on a high-voltage line without current flowing through its body to ground?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Copper has very low resistance and insulation blocks the wiper contact, so a rheostat requires bare nichrome wire or graphite.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping thick insulated copper hookup wire around a dowel creates an effective variable resistor for dimming a flashlight bulb.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A single-pole, double-throw switch routes one common input terminal to either of two selectable output paths.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A single-pole, double-throw switch controls two completely separate battery sources at the exact same time.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Leaving half the enamel on one axle lead acts as a commutator that cuts current each half-turn so magnetic torque stays in one direction.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stripping every bit of enamel from both axle leads of a simple wire-coil motor makes the coil spin faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wiring a switch directly across battery terminals creates a dead short when closed; the switch must be wired in series with the load.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A switch must be wired across the positive and negative battery terminals in parallel with the buzzer to turn it off.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a homemade DC motor's rotation if you sand all the insulating enamel off both ends of the coil wire?
Where should a Scout connect the battery feed on a single-pole, double-throw switch to alternate between two lamps?
Which physical change in your pencil-lead or nichrome rheostat dims the test bulb as you slide the wiper clip?
Why is it dangerous to leave a homemade motor coil stalled across a lantern battery when the rotor stops spinning?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most electrical apprenticeships use an earn-while-you-learn model where apprentices receive hourly wages while completing field hours.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Entering a trade union or contractor electrical apprenticeship requires paying four years of university tuition before earning pay.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Installing building wiring legally requires a state electrician license earned through supervised field hours and code exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating with a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering automatically grants a state license to wire residential homes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Apprentices must work under a licensed journeyman or master electrician, and pulling permits typically requires a master license.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A newly indentured first-year electrical apprentice can legally pull municipal building permits and work unsupervised on job sites.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most states require licensed electricians to take continuing education courses whenever the National Electrical Code is updated.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Once an electrician passes the initial journeyman exam, their license remains valid for life without further code training.

extra_socratic_questions: What combination of classroom instruction and supervised on-the-job hours is required to qualify for a journeyman exam?
Which daily responsibilities separate a licensed inside wireman from a utility lineworker or an electrical engineer?
What out-of-pocket expenses for insulated hand tools, boots, and licensing fees should an apprentice budget in year one?
Why must licensed electricians complete continuing education on National Electrical Code updates to keep their credentials?
